items: Joining a fight already going, you see it as it stands: torches knocked down or put out, crates burnt, wagons shoved, burning or gone.
The yard: right click parries, Z X R do the forms of your weapon, as in a fight.
Friends in the camp see your practice in the yard: your blows, weaves, bursts and rolls.
A man's Healing is open from book 3, like a woman's (still woven with his own flows).
Channellers can open their weave tree in the camp (T, or the sheet's button), with the bar along the bottom to drag things on and off.
Running in the camp eases in and out at a fight's pace, as it does in a fight.
On the server, fights on different maps at once each keep their own ground (one could end up fought on another's map).
Forms have their own row beside the bar, for the weapon in your hand: Z, X, R, then Shift and a number. Each is drawn as the path it cuts.
Fire Arrow: a bow form that bursts where it strikes and leaves them burning.
Balefire, the Lash of Water and Hammer of Air go where you aim them, up a slope or down off a wall.
Maps are bigger and closed by cliffs you can see: both ends of Tarwin's Gap, a ring of hills round the wagon ring and the open fields, a palisade round the camp.
Ledges and plateaus: ramps up, steep sides you cannot walk up, low shelves you can jump onto. Shelves along the walls of Tarwin's Gap.
A new place in every doorway: the Watch Hill, a flat-topped hill in the Borderland hills, attacked from every side.
Trollocs hate water: they go round a stream if they can and balk at the bank, unless a Myrddraal drives them on.
Enemies stuck behind a tree or a wall's end find the way round.
First person: your head still casts its shadow, and looking down you see your chest, arms and legs.
The armoury, tailor and study block you as their shapes; tent ropes no longer hang upside down.
Lightning arcs between enemies are seen online again (they were being dropped).
The camp is the training yard: practice posts to the west of the doorways; click to strike or weave at them, Space to roll. Nobody else in the camp can be struck. (No more training doorway.)

Things react to the fight: Air knocks torches flat and shoves them, puts torches and fires out; Fire lights them again; crates and barrels are shoved, burnt or smashed; wagons shoved, set alight (they burn down) or wrecked.
Waves grow for a stronger channeller and for every friend who joins, and never shrink back.
The tree pages have your bar along the bottom: drag things on, along and off, and choose whether new things go on by themselves.
With the sheet put away, a faded corner keeps your name and renown, and a mark when something is new.
Balefire needs the first weave of every Power. A man's Healing uses his own flows (Spirit, Fire and Earth) and is drawn in them.
This list, under Esc.
Bow and thrown forms: Snap Shot, Two on the String, Through the Line, Hail of Shafts, the Heart Shot; Flick of the Wrist, a Fan of Steel, Hard and Low, the Gleeman's Juggle.
Channellers work out the chosen weave between rounds by what they channel, won or lost.
The Esc menu shows your version, the server's, and each friend's.
Dream duels: a friend still at the doorway no longer ends the duel; alone, your shade comes (on the server too); only the winner is told they won.
The server proves it knows the word before your game sends anything.
Twenty forms that used a stand-in punch have their own arm strokes; flurries change hands blow by blow.
The weapon and form trees fit the screen however long a column grows.
Much faster: about twice the frame rate in a big fight, half the draw calls; the camp a quarter.
Picture quality Medium and Low now also lighten shadows, ambient shading and anti-aliasing.
The standalone keeps its data beside the executable again.
Going down: you stay down until the wave ends; a friend beside you then brings you back at 1 health, otherwise you die. Healing gets you up at once.
Damage numbers, bigger and brighter the harder the hit.
Enemies leave the downed alone; bot channellers need to see you, pause between weaves and miss sometimes.
Fighters have two trees, weapons and forms; a better weapon of a kind replaces the old one.
Men who channel start with a short sword.
Installed games update themselves.
